question: On 16 July 2025, India achieved a major milestone by successfully destroying two aerial high-speed unmanned targets at high altitude in Ladakh using the upgraded variant of the Akash Weapon System for the Indian Army called ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Akash Prime**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On **16 July 2025**, India successfully destroyed two high-speed unmanned aerial targets at high altitude in the Ladakh region, marking a significant milestone in the country's defense capabilities.
 
• This achievement was accomplished using the **Akash Prime**, the upgraded variant of the Akash Weapon System designed specifically for the **Indian Army**.
 
• The **Akash Prime** is an advanced surface-to-air missile system that incorporates several improvements over its predecessor, including enhanced guidance systems, better accuracy, and the ability to operate in extreme weather conditions.
 
• The test conducted in Ladakh demonstrated the **system's capability to neutralize aerial threats at high altitudes**, making it particularly suitable for defending India's borders in mountainous regions.
 
• The Akash Weapon System, including its **Prime variant**, is part of India’s push toward achieving self-reliance in defense technology under the **‘Make in India’ initiative.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Akash Prime:**

 
 
• The **Akash Prime** is an upgraded version of the Akash surface-to-air missile system developed by the **Defense Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)**.
 
• It is equipped with an **indigenously developed active RF seeker** for improved target tracking and interception.
 
• The system is capable of engaging multiple targets simultaneously and can operate in a variety of challenging environments.
 
• The Akash Prime can target **enemy aircraft, drones, and cruise missiles**, providing a robust layer of defense.
 
 
 
• **BrahMos:**
 
 
• The **BrahMos** is a supersonic cruise missile developed jointly by India and Russia.
 
• It is known for its high speed, precision, and ability to be launched from land, sea, and air platforms.
 
• Unlike Akash Prime, BrahMos is primarily an offensive missile designed for precision strikes on ground and naval targets.
 
 
 
• **Pinaka:**
 
 
• **Pinaka** is a multi-barrel rocket launcher system developed by DRDO and is used by the Indian Army.
 
• It is designed for area saturation and is capable of launching a salvo of rockets in a short period to neutralize enemy positions.
 
• Pinaka is not a surface-to-air missile system and thus is not relevant to countering aerial threats.
 
 
 
• **Other Akash Variants:**
 
 
• The original **Akash Weapon System** was developed as a medium-range surface-to-air missile system for the Indian Armed Forces.
 
• It has been deployed by both the **Indian Army and Air Force** to provide air defense against enemy aircraft and missiles.
 
• The **Akash Advanced** is another variant focused on enhanced range and lethality, but it lacks some of the specific advancements found in Akash Prime.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Test:**
 
 
• The successful test of Akash Prime in Ladakh underscores India’s capability to defend its high-altitude borders effectively.
 
• It reflects the growing indigenization of defense technology under the **‘Atmanirbhar Bharat’ initiative**.
 
• With advanced systems like Akash Prime, India strengthens its preparedness against aerial threats in high-altitude regions like **Ladakh**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **DRDO’s Role:**

 
 
• The **Defense Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)** is the primary agency behind the design and development of the Akash Weapon System and its variants.
 
• DRDO is a key player in India’s defense self-reliance initiatives, producing a range of weapon systems and technologies.
 
 
 
• **High-Altitude Defense:**
 
 
• High-altitude regions like Ladakh pose unique challenges for defense systems due to thin air, extreme temperatures, and rugged terrain.
 
• The Akash Prime’s successful test in this environment demonstrates its suitability for deployment in such areas.
 
 
 
• **Make in India Initiative:**
 
 
• The Akash Prime is a product of India’s **‘Make in India’ initiative**, which aims to reduce dependence on foreign defense imports.
 
• It also highlights India’s capability to develop advanced technologies indigenously.
